findings.finding: MBA weekly data show the Q3 mortgage market weakening well beyond the July guide. Week ending 7 Aug: refi -22% and purchase -1% YoY. Week ending 28 Aug: refi -19%, purchase ~0%. Week ending 25 Sep: refi -56% and purchase -14% YoY, with the 30y at 7.3%. Equifax's Q3 guide assumed originations down only low single digits and US mortgage revenue up about 20%, so Q3 mortgage inquiries (and the ~25% of revenue that is US mortgage) likely land below the guide's assumption, against a Q3 2025 base boosted by a September 2025 refi spike.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2023: mortgage inquiries fell 29% vs a -23% guide and the stock fell ~6% on the FY cut. Q3 2025: inquiries -7% vs a feared -12% and the stock moved only -0.51%. Q1 2026 beat on mortgage (+38%) but fell -3.04%. This name has not paid for reported-quarter mortgage beats, but it has sold off on mortgage misses that carry into the guide.

findings.finding: The 30y mortgage rate was 7.4% on 15 Oct 2026 (highest since Nov 2023), against roughly 6.6% embedded in the July FY guide (management: 'current mortgage rates are what is embedded'). Q4 2025 had a refi-heavy base at ~6.2-6.3%, so the implied Q4 guide (~$2.23 adj EPS at the FY midpoint, and ~$2.22 in FY consensus of $8.53) is likely cut when Equifax gives its Q4 outlook on 20 Oct.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guide-driven: Q2 2025 -8.18% on the outlook; Q2 2026 -3.93% (about -7% intraday per the sweep) on a below-consensus Q3 guide despite an EPS beat; Oct 2023 about -6% on a mortgage-driven FY cut. Five of seven prints in the baseline fell.

findings.finding: US hiring is weakening into the quarter. September payrolls were +29k vs ~90k expected, July was revised to -10k and August cut to +133k, and unemployment rose to 4.2%. That weighs on EWS Talent Solutions (already declining in Q2) and non-mortgage verification volumes, against a Q3 guide for diversified markets up mid-single digits.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2024/Q4 2024: hiring weakness in EWS Talent was repeatedly cited in guide trims; there is no clean isolated reaction in the baseline.

findings.finding: The +8.4% five-session run-up is a sector relief rally (TRU +10.7%, Experian +7%, EFX +7.25% on 15 Oct) after FHFA Director Pulte skipped MBA Annual without the expected tri-merge to bi-merge announcement. The overhang stays open: MBA's CEO said he is 'increasingly confident that tri-merge won't be around for long'. So EFX goes into the print 11-12% off its early-October low with no company news behind the bounce.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: EFX fell ~4% on 29 Sep (unified VantageScore grid) and ~4% the week of 1 Oct (Bloomberg bi-merge report), then gained 7.25% on 15 Oct. Regulatory headlines move it 4-7% in a day.

findings.finding: On 29 Sep 2026 FHFA put VantageScore 4.0 on the same LLPA grid as Classic FICO. The bureaus priced VantageScore at about $1 (TRU at $0.99 through Dec 2028), and TRU said VantageScore was already in ~30% of its mortgage inquiries by Q2. Equifax's 2026 guide assumes it keeps selling FICO scores for all 2026 mortgage transactions, with limited VantageScore revenue, so any lender switching in Q4 lowers reported mortgage revenue (FICO pass-through) and muddies the Q4/2027 outlook.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: EFX fell 4.1% pre-market (closed -3%) on the 29 Sep grid announcement. The FICO direct-license news in Oct 2025 also hit the bureaus.

findings.finding: EWS government verification was guided to return to growth in 2H 2026, with ~$300M of new annual contract value signed (mostly a 2027 benefit, some in 2H26) and a pipeline about 2x the year-ago level. Medicaid/SNAP work requirements from Jan 2027 give Equifax room to talk up 2027 on the call.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Government verification was the swing line in 2025 prints (Q2 2025 -8.18% partly on a government slowdown). No clean positive reaction on this line in the baseline.

findings.finding: Equifax has beaten consensus EPS four quarters running (avg ~5%), and Q2 2026 came in $0.05 above the guide midpoint. It doubled its AI-driven cost-reduction target to $150m (2026 savings in guide), giving a cost lever to hold Q3 EPS near $2.20 even with a mortgage revenue shortfall.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Beats are sold: Q1 2026 beat by ~10% ($1.86 vs ~$1.70) and the stock fell -3.04%; Q2 2026 beat by $0.05 and it fell -3.93%.

findings.finding: Six price-target cuts cluster in 2-19 Oct 2026, ahead of the print: Barclays 200 to 155 (EW, citing negative sector sentiment), Goldman 171 to 148 (Neutral), BofA 210 to 200, Morgan Stanley 225 to 205, RBC 194 to 177 (higher rates, consumer lending, credit-reporting rule risk), Mizuho 210 to 185 on 19 Oct. That lowers the sentiment bar into a guide cut.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q4 2025 print (Feb 2026, +3.42%) came after a heavy de-rating; reaction history after pre-print PT-cut clusters is not isolated in the baseline.

findings.finding: Equifax issued $1bn of senior notes (5.000% 2029, 5.650% 2033) on 29 Jul 2026 to repay commercial paper, and Círculo de Crédito ($750m EV) is expected to close in Q4 2026. The financing term-outs existing CP and pre-funds the acquisition, and is not distress; 2H buybacks continue at a slower pace with leverage below 3x.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None isolated.

findings.finding: A $100m class settlement over the 2022 'OMS' credit-score coding error got preliminary approval on 17 Aug 2026 (final hearing 22 Jan 2027). It will likely appear as a legal charge excluded from adjusted EPS.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Legal charges are excluded from adjusted EPS and have not moved EFX prints.

outside_window.finding: A formal FHFA tri-merge to bi-merge directive for Fannie/Freddie deliveries ('within weeks' per Bloomberg; Pulte skipped the MBA Annual slot). Timing is undated and unlikely to land exactly in the 20 Oct session; William Blair puts EFX tri-merge-linked revenue at ~$270m.
Medicaid/SNAP work requirements take effect Jan 2027, with more frequent Work Number checks: a 2027 revenue driver for EWS government.
TransUnion Q3 2026 print, expected after EFX, gives a peer read on mortgage inquiries; it lands after the exit window.

Lesson 1 (verified fact is not a reaction; this name sells beats): beat-track/AI-savings finding cut from +0.3 to +0.2.
